longTitle.officialTitle: To redesignate the Chiricahua National Monument in the State of Arizona as Chiricahua National Park, and for other purposes.

main.enactingFormula: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

section.heading: SHORT TITLE.
section.content: This Act may be cited as the “Chiricahua National Park Act”.

section.heading: DESIGNATION OF CHIRICAHUA NATIONAL PARK, ARIZONA.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Chiricahua National Monument in the State of Arizona established by Presidential Proclamation 1692 (54 U.S.C. 320301 note; 43 Stat. 1946) shall be known and designated as “Chiricahua National Park” (referred to in this Act as the “National Park”).

paragraph.heading: Boundaries.—
paragraph.content: The boundaries of the National Park shall be the boundaries of the Chiricahua National Monument as of the date of enactment of this Act, as generally depicted on the map entitled “Chiricahua National Park Proposed Boundary”, numbered 145/156,356, and dated March 2021.

paragraph.heading: References.—
paragraph.content: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, or other record of the United States to the Chiricahua National Monument shall be considered to be a reference to the “Chiricahua National Park”.

paragraph.heading: Availability of funds.—
paragraph.content: Any funds available for the Chiricahua National Monument shall be available for the National Park.

subsection.heading: Administration.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary of the Interior shall administer the National Park in accordance with—

paragraph.content: Presidential Proclamation 2288 (54 U.S.C. 320301 note; 52 Stat. 1551); and

paragraph.chapeau: the laws generally applicable to units of the National Park System, including—

subparagraph.content: section 100101(a), chapter 1003, and sections 100751(a), 100752, 100753, and 102101 of title 54, United States Code; and
chapter 3201 of title 54, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall ensure the protection of traditional cultural and religious sites in the National Park in accordance with the laws (including regulations) applicable to the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Consultation.—
paragraph.content: In carrying out paragraph (1), the Secretary shall consult with Indian Tribes in accordance with laws applicable to the protection of cultural and religious sites.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary, in accordance with Public Law 95-341 (42 U.S.C. 1996 et seq.)—

subparagraph.content: shall provide access to the sites described in subsection (a)(1) by members of Indian Tribes for traditional cultural and customary uses; and

may, on request of an Indian Tribe, temporarily close to general public use one or more specific areas of the National Park to protect traditional cultural and customary uses in the area by members of the Indian Tribe.

paragraph.heading: Limitation.—
paragraph.content: In closing a portion of a designated area under paragraph (1)(B), the Secretary shall limit the closure to the smallest practicable area for the minimum period necessary for the traditional cultural and religious activities.

paragraph.heading: Indian tribe.—
paragraph.content: The term “Indian Tribe” has the meaning given such term in section 4 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5304).

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.
